cards.title: Practice drawing (made-up, not a real MTU document)
cards.simple: A made-up panel used to show how the cards work. Replace it with cards from your real drawings.

cards.title: Practice panel: engine running indication
cards.simple: When the engine runs, PLC A1 switches output DO4. DO4 energises relay K12, and K12 contact 13-14 lights lamp H5 on the panel door.

cards.title: H5 engine running lamp
cards.simple: 24V LED indicator lamp on the panel door, lit while the engine is running. Wired to X2:5 (+) and X2:6 (0V).

cards.title: K12 running relay
cards.simple: 24V DC relay. Coil A1-A2 is driven by PLC output DO4. NO contact 13-14 switches the running lamp H5. Coil should measure roughly the value on its label (often a few hundred Ω).

cards.title: F3 indication fuse
cards.simple: 2 A fuse feeding the indication circuit (lamp H5 through K12).

cards.title: F2 PLC output fuse
cards.simple: Fuse feeding the PLC A1 output group, including DO4.

cards.title: A1 PLC (output DO4)
cards.simple: Controller that switches DO4 ON when it detects the engine is running. DO4 is a 24V sourcing output that energises K12.

cards.title: X2 terminal strip
cards.simple: Door wiring terminals. X2:5 = lamp H5 positive, X2:6 = lamp H5 return to 0V.

cards.title: H5 running lamp circuit
cards.control: K12 coil, energised by PLC A1 output DO4 (see CKT-002)
cards.simple: H5 lights when K12 is pulled in, closing contact 13-14.

cards.title: K12 relay coil circuit
cards.simple: PLC A1 turns DO4 on when the engine is running, which energises the K12 coil.

cards.title: H5 running lamp not glowing
cards.simple: Engine is running but H5 stays dark.
checks: Is the engine really running and does the PLC see it? Check A1 status / DO4 LED.
Is K12 pulled in? Listen or feel for the click, check the relay's flag/LED. Not pulled in → go to F-002.
Measure X2:5 to 0V. 24V present → H5 or its return is the fault (go to the last two steps).
No voltage at X2:5: measure across K12 13-14. Full 24V across it → contact open (worn relay).
Still nothing: check fuse F3 and its supply.
Measure directly across H5 (X2:5 to X2:6). 24V across it but dark → lamp faulty.
24V at X2:5 but not across H5 → return X2:6 to 0V is open.

cards.title: K12 relay not pulling in
cards.simple: PLC output DO4 should be on but the relay does not switch.
checks: Is the A1 DO4 LED on? If off, the PLC is not commanding it: check why the PLC doesn't see engine running.
LED on: measure DO4 terminal to 0V. No 24V → check fuse F2, then the PLC output itself.
24V at DO4: measure K12:A1 to K12:A2. 24V across the coil but no pull-in → relay faulty.
24V at A1 but not across A1-A2 → K12:A2 return to 0V is open.
Power off: measure coil resistance. Open = coil burnt. Near 0 Ω = shorted (and may blow F2).

cards.title: 4-20 mA sensor shows fault or minimum value
cards.simple: A generic check for any loop-powered analog sensor.
checks: Read the actual loop current (in series) or the input's diagnostic value.
About 0 mA → open loop: check the sensor's supply voltage, plugs and wires.
Steady 4 mA but the process is clearly not at minimum → sensor stuck or wrongly ranged.
Above 20.5 mA → short or over-range: check for wires shorted together.
Compare with a gauge or a known good sensor if possible.

cards.title: CAN bus communication fault
cards.simple: A generic check when controllers lose contact over CAN.
checks: Power off: measure CAN-H to CAN-L. About 60 Ω OK, about 120 Ω = one terminator missing, near 0 Ω = short, open = break.
Check each plug on the bus for pushed-back pins or water.
Power on: CAN-H about 2.5-3.5V, CAN-L about 1.5-2.5V to ground.
Unplug devices one by one to find one that pulls the bus down.
